claims.text: In Pulumi, a package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside a package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide, and following them improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry requires applying a semver Git tag (e.g., `v1.2.3`) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are supported and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components in that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) for distinct packages.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Pulumi Amazon EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` file at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it (e.g., in a `components/` directory).
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
It is technically possible to use a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.

In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA releases the package at v1.1.0 and a subsequent breaking change to ComponentB releases the package at v2.0.0, per semver conventions (minor bump for feature, major bump for breaking change).

The Pulumi IDP Private Registry is documented at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/ and `pulumi package publish` is documented at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/ (link targets must exist).

Linked pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/packages/, /docs/iac/concepts/components/, /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/packaging-components/ (anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages), and /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
